newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cites threat to confidence in Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cites threat to confidence in Hong Kong.

text.p: The United States voiced deep concern on Monday over what it called new steps to water down civil liberties in Hong Kong, citing the move as a threat to confidence at home and abroad after Hong Kong reverts to China's control.

State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said the protection of civil liberties was a critical component of Hong Kong's way of life "and we believe it is vital to continue both confidence within Hong Kong after July 1, 1997, and also international confidence in Hong Kong."
China resumes control of Hong Kong at midnight on June 30 after 150 years of British colonial rule.

The Beijing-selected Preparatory Committee responsible for re-imposing Chinese sovereignty over Hong Kong voted on Saturday to roll back some of the territory's laws, including part of its Bill of Rights, on grounds of inconsistency with China's Basic Law for Hong Kong.

"The United States is deeply concerned by the attempts to weaken these civil liberties and these basic freedoms in Hong Kong, and any recommendations of this type made over the weekend do not help foster confidence and stability in Hong Kong itself," Burns told a regular news briefing.

"Therefore, we will continue to convey to the Chinese authorities in Beijing, and to future Hong Kong government authorities as well, the importance that the United States attaches to China's actions in upholding its commitments for Hong Kong," he said.
